project.vehicle_programs: Platform analyzed as a Safety Element out of Context (ISO 26262-10 §9). First configuration: 2020 Toyota Corolla LE (U.S.), opendbc platform TOYOTA_COROLLA_TSS2. Target ASIL D is a provisional planning assumption pending the HARA.

tailoring.justification: Safety plan, safety culture, confirmation measures and safety case. Independence requirements cannot currently be met (single maintainer); confirmation reviews are blocked until independent reviewers are recruited.
Item definition, HARA, safety goals and functional safety concept, at platform level (SEooC) with assumptions verified per vehicle configuration.
Technical safety concept, item integration and testing, safety validation.
Applies to the panda and harness only. Vehicle ECUs are outside the item. The comma device application processor is QM; safety relies on the panda checker.
Full rigor for the panda firmware and brand safety modes. openpilot driving software is argued as QM behind the checker, subject to the independence argument in the TSC.
Research platform; no production. Revisit before any hardware distribution or field deployment.

Configuration and change management, verification, documentation, tool qualification (Clause 11), qualification of existing software (Clause 12). Clause 5 distributed development: no DIA possible with upstream; treated as qualification of existing software.
Possible ASIL decomposition between the openpilot stack and the panda checker; dependent-failure analysis to support it.
Safety Element out of Context approach (Clause 9) for the platform.
Consulted for the panda microcontroller's safety mechanisms and failure modes.
Passenger cars and light SUVs only.

tools.name: arm-none-eabi-gcc
tools.version: As pinned by the panda build
tools.tcl_rationale: TI2: a compiler error can introduce a fault in safety firmware. TD3 until a detection argument exists. Planned route to TCL2: back-to-back testing of the compiled firmware against the host-built libsafety on the same test vectors, plus HIL.

tools.name: cppcheck MISRA addon
tools.usage: MISRA C:2012 checking of safety code
tools.tcl_rationale: TI2: a missed violation could hide a defect. TD2: code review and unit tests also catch most defects such a rule targets.

tools.name: Python unittest + libsafety harness
tools.usage: Unit tests of brand safety modes; source of coverage data
tools.tcl_rationale: TI2: a harness bug could report a false pass. TD2: mutation testing checks that the tests detect injected faults.

tools.name: gcov
tools.usage: Structural coverage of the safety layer
tools.tcl_rationale: TI2: overstated coverage could hide untested code. TD2: cross-checked by mutation analysis and the independent XZACT equivalence coverage report.

tools.name: Mutation test harness (opendbc test_mutation.py)
tools.usage: Checks that the safety tests detect injected faults
tools.tcl_rationale: TI1 for the product: it can only report weak tests, not introduce or hide a product defect.

tools.name: XZACT compiler and equivalence harness
tools.usage: Independent re-implementation of the Toyota safety mode, used as diverse evidence of its behavior
tools.tcl_rationale: TI1 while used only as independent evidence: a fault in the port or compiler causes a mismatch against the original C, not a hidden product defect. Becomes TCL3 if XZACT-generated code is ever used in the product; known silent-miscompile issues would then block it.

tools.name: openpilot process replay
tools.usage: Regression detection by replaying recorded drives
tools.tcl_rationale: TI2: a false 'no change' result could let a regression through. TD2: complemented by unit tests and on-road validation.

tools.name: tinygrad
tools.usage: Compiles and runs the driving and driver-monitoring models
tools.tcl_rationale: Affects learned components argued under ISO 21448 and ISO/PAS 8800; classification depends on the TSC independence argument.

tools.name: SCons, GitHub Actions, Jenkins
tools.tcl_rationale: TI1 for the product: build and CI faults surface as build or test failures, verified by checksums and test results.

tools.name: Git and GitHub
tools.usage: Configuration management, review, traceability of changes
tools.tcl_rationale: Supports configuration management (26262-8 §7); does not produce product content.

anomaly_process: Anomalies are tracked as GitHub issues labelled 'safety-anomaly' and mirrored here at each plan revision. Each is assessed for impact on safety goals, requirements and evidence (ISO 26262-8 §8), assigned an owner, and closed only with linked evidence. An anomaly that affects a released work product reopens that work product's confirmation review.

anomalies.description: No independent reviewers: ASIL D work products need I3 confirmation reviews, and the project has a single maintainer.
anomalies.resolution: Recruit independent reviewers (milestone M05). Until then no confirmation review can close.

anomalies.description: The XZACT compiler silently miscompiled valid programs (Otherwise bound to a nested If; shared text buffers; out-of-order top-level Let). See XZACT-Lang apps/openpilot_toyota_safety/README.md.
anomalies.resolution: No product impact while XZACT is used only as independent evidence (TCL1): a miscompile shows up as a mismatch. Blocks any use of XZACT-generated code in the product.

anomalies.description: No development interface agreement is possible with upstream (comma.ai). Upstream changes arrive through submodule pins without a supplier safety case.
anomalies.resolution: Treat upstream as existing software (ISO 26262-8 §12): pin commits, impact-analyze every pin update, and qualify the safety layer with LionDriver's own evidence.

anomalies.description: Target ASIL D is a planning assumption made before the HARA.
anomalies.resolution: Draft HARA LD-HARA-001 0.1 yields five ASIL D safety goals (SG-001 to SG-005), consistent with the target. Closes when the HARA passes its confirmation review.

anomalies.description: panda microcontroller fault detection is insufficient for ASIL D: a software watchdog on the main loop and interrupt-rate monitoring only record faults; no lockstep core or independent hardware watchdog; no evidence that a recorded fault leads to a no-output state (FSC gap G1).
anomalies.resolution: Assess the STM32H7's safety mechanisms; decide on an external watchdog with relay cut-off and/or a second monitoring MCU in the TSC. Blocks the D(D) + QM(D) decomposition.
